column1: # topic: Chapter 1: The First Civilizations of North America
What natural obstacles left Native Americans vulnerable when they met Europeans?
column2: The north-south axis slowed the spread of crops and technology, and the scarcity of domesticated animals left Native Americans without immunity to Eurasian diseases.

column1: Why do archaeologists no longer accept the "Clovis first" theory?
column2: Sites such as Monte Verde in Chile and Buttermilk Creek in Texas are older than any Clovis site, proving that people reached the Americas before the Clovis culture.

column1: How did Eastern Woodlands subsistence differ from Mesoamerican subsistence?
column2: Mesoamericans depended on farming that supported large cities, while most Eastern Woodlands peoples lived by fishing, gathering, and hunting and never adopted agriculture.

column1: How did Mesoamerica influence the peoples of the Southwest?
column2: Mesoamerican farming spread north to the Southwest, and some Southwestern architectural styles came to clearly resemble those of Mexico.
